source.text: וַיִּקְרְב֥וּ יְמֵֽי־דָוִ֖ד לָמ֑וּת וַיְצַ֛ו אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And drew near [the] days of David to die, and he charged Solomon his son, saying,

en.L: And the days of David drew near to die, and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
en.B: When the time came near for David to die, he gave a charge to his son Solomon:
en.R: When David was about to die, he gave his son Solomon these orders:

decisions.choice: the days drew near to die: his death was close
decisions.reason: "His days drew near to die" is a way of saying that someone's death is near, used of Jacob (Genesis 47:29) and of Moses (Deuteronomy 31:14).

decisions.choice: charged: gave his last instructions
decisions.reason: The verb means to give orders. Here, as when Jacob finished charging his sons before he died (Genesis 49:33), it is a dying man's final charge, something like a spoken will. It covers both David's religious charge (verses 2-4) and his instructions about particular men (verses 5-9).

decisions.choice: When the time came near for David to die; When David was about to die
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Hebrew picture of days drawing near into a plain statement about time.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחָזַקְתָּ֖ וְהָיִ֥יתָֽ לְאִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: I [am] going in [the] way of all the earth; and you shall be strong and shall become a man,

en.L: "I [am] going in the way of all the earth; so be strong and become a man.
en.B: "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, then, and show yourself a man.
en.R: "I am about to die, as everyone on earth must. So be strong, and show that you are a man.

decisions.choice: going in the way of all the earth: about to die
decisions.reason: The same words are Joshua's at the end of his life (Joshua 23:14). Death is the road that everyone on earth walks.

decisions.choice: become a man: act with a man's courage and steadiness
decisions.reason: "Be a man" calls for courage and firmness, as when the Philistines urged each other, "Be men and fight" (1 Samuel 4:9). Solomon was young (3:7), and the hard tasks of verses 5-9 lay ahead of him. The phrase is about maturity and nerve, not about age or strength of body.

decisions.choice: you shall be strong and become: commands
decisions.reason: The verbs are in a form that, after David's statement, carries the force of a command: in view of his coming death, Solomon must be strong.

decisions.choice: show yourself a man
decisions.reason: Balanced says "show yourself a man" so that the phrase is heard as a call to act, not as a statement about becoming an adult.

decisions.choice: I am about to die, as everyone on earth must
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom in plain words.

source.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לָלֶ֤כֶת בִּדְרָכָיו֙ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר חֻקֹּתָ֤יו מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֣יו וְעֵדְוֺתָ֔יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֗יל אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּפְנֶ֖ה שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: and keep [the] charge of Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments and his judgments and his testimonies, as [is] written in [the] law of Moses, so that you may act wisely [in] all that you do and [in] all where you turn there,

en.L: And keep the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies, as [it is] written in the law of Moses, so that you may act wisely in all that you do and everywhere that you turn,
en.B: Keep what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has entrusted to you: walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees, as they are written in the law of Moses. Then you will act wisely and succeed in all you do and wherever you turn,
en.R: Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you to do. Live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants you to live, and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws, commands, rules, and instructions, as they are written in the teaching of Moses. Then you will be wise and do well in everything you do and wherever you go.

decisions.choice: keep the charge of Yahweh: carry out the duty Yahweh has entrusted
decisions.reason: The noun names a duty or trust that someone is set to guard (Genesis 26:5; Leviticus 8:35; Deuteronomy 11:1). The verb "keep" and the noun come from the same root: Solomon is to guard what Yahweh has given him to guard.

decisions.choice: statutes, commandments, judgments, testimonies: the whole of Yahweh's covenant requirements
decisions.reason: The four words overlap and together mean everything the covenant asks, as such lists do in Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 6:1-2; 8:11; 11:1). The testimonies are the covenant terms solemnly declared and witnessed.

decisions.choice: as written in the law of Moses; so that you may act wisely: words from Deuteronomy and Joshua
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy tells the king to keep a written copy of the law and read it all his life (Deuteronomy 17:18-20). The promise that keeping the law brings wise action and success echoes Deuteronomy 29:8 and Yahweh's charge to Joshua (Joshua 1:7-8), who was also told to be strong.

decisions.choice: act wisely: act with insight, and so succeed
decisions.reason: The verb means to have insight and act on it; success follows from it (1 Samuel 18:14-15). Both sides of the word are meant here.

decisions.choice: statutes, commandments, judgments, testimonies / statutes, commandments, rulings, decrees / laws, commands, rules, instructions
decisions.reason: The four terms follow the wording settled for these words across the books from Exodus on, at each level.

decisions.choice: the teaching of Moses
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the law of Moses, as in Deuteronomy, because the word covers instruction for all of life, not only rules.

source.text: לְמַעַן֩ יָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַי֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם־יִשְׁמְר֨וּ בָנֶ֜יךָ אֶת־דַּרְכָּ֗ם לָלֶ֤כֶת לְפָנַי֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת בְּכָל־לְבָבָ֖ם וּבְכָל־נַפְשָׁ֑ם לֵאמֹ֕ר לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: so that may establish Yahweh his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, If keep your sons their way, to walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul, saying, not will be cut off for you a man from on [the] throne of Israel.

en.L: so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may establish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons keep their way, to walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their soul,' saying, 'a man will not be cut off for you from on the throne of Israel.'
en.B: so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may keep the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made about me: 'If your descendants watch how they live, walking faithfully before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all their heart and all their soul, there will always be a man of your line on the throne of Israel.'
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will keep the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to me. He said, 'Your descendants must be careful to live faithfully for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all their heart and soul. If they do, one of your family will always sit on Israel's throne.'

decisions.choice: his word about me: the promise of 2 Samuel 7:12-16
decisions.reason: Through Nathan, Yahweh promised David a son who would build a house for his name and a throne that would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). Here David speaks of the promise with a condition attached, as Psalm 132:12 does and as Yahweh will repeat to Solomon (1 Kings 8:25; 9:4-5). The promise to David's line stands, but each king who sits on the throne must keep faith.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness: with loyal, true conduct
decisions.reason: The word means firmness and reliability, truth lived out. To walk before Yahweh in it is to serve him loyally and honestly (Joshua 24:14; 1 Samuel 12:24).

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you from the throne: your line will always have a king
decisions.reason: The negative idiom means that David's line will never lack a descendant to reign (8:25; 9:5; Jeremiah 33:17).

decisions.choice: saying: the quotation resumes
decisions.reason: After the long condition, the word "saying" is repeated to pick up the quotation again. It does not start a second promise.

decisions.choice: your descendants; there will always be a man of your line
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "descendants" because the sons meant are all David's heirs in later generations, and turn the negative "will not be cut off" into a positive statement.

decisions.choice: Your descendants must be careful ... If they do
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into two short sentences.

source.text: וְגַ֣ם אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֨שָׂה לִ֜י יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֣י צִבְא֣וֹת יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לְאַבְנֵ֨ר בֶּן־נֵ֜ר וְלַעֲמָשָׂ֤א בֶן־יֶ֨תֶר֙ וַיַּ֣הַרְגֵ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דְּמֵֽי־מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֞ן דְּמֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֗ה בַּחֲגֹֽרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמָתְנָ֔יו וּֽבְנַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And also you know what did to me Joab son of Zeruiah, what he did to [the] two commanders of [the] armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether, and he killed them and put blood of war in peace, and put blood of war on his belt which [was] on his waist and in his sandals which [were] on his feet.

en.L: And you also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether: he killed them, and put [the] blood of war in peace, and put [the] blood of war on his belt that [was] around his waist and in his sandals that [were] on his feet.
en.B: You also know how Joab son of Zeruiah treated me, and what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, spilling blood in a time of peace as though it were war, and he stained the belt at his waist and the sandals on his feet with that blood of war.
en.R: You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me. You know what he did to two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He murdered them when there was no war, as if they were enemies in battle. Their blood was on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.

decisions.choice: Abner and Amasa: Joab's two murders
decisions.reason: Joab killed Abner, Saul's former commander, after David had made peace with him (2 Samuel 3:22-30), and he killed Amasa, whom David had made commander of the army (2 Samuel 19:14; 20:8-10). Both men were killed in peacetime by a man pretending friendship.

decisions.choice: what Joab did to me: the two murders
alternatives: other wrongs as well, such as killing Absalom
decisions.reason: The second "what he did" spells out the first: by killing these men Joab wronged David, who had given them his word and was blamed for their deaths (2 Samuel 3:28-39). Joab's killing of Absalom against David's orders (2 Samuel 18:5, 14) may also be in mind, but the verse names only the two murders.

decisions.choice: put blood of war in peace: shed in peacetime the blood that belongs only to battle
decisions.reason: Killing in war was not murder, but Joab killed these men when there was no war. He treated a time of peace as a battlefield, so the killings were murder.

decisions.choice: blood of war on his belt and sandals: the guilt marked him
decisions.reason: Joab stabbed Amasa with a sword that slipped from his belt (2 Samuel 20:8-10), so the blood was on him in a plain sense. The picture also says that the guilt clings to Joab from his waist to his feet.

decisions.choice: Joab son of Zeruiah: David's nephew
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel are always named after her. Joab had commanded David's army for most of his reign (2 Samuel 8:16).

decisions.choice: murdered; when there was no war, as if they were enemies in battle
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase "put blood of war in peace" in plain words.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כְּחָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־תוֹרֵ֧ד שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּשָׁלֹ֖ם שְׁאֹֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And act according to your wisdom, and not bring down his gray head in peace [to] Sheol.

en.L: So act according to your wisdom, and do not bring down his gray head in peace [to] Sheol.
en.B: Act as your wisdom tells you, but do not allow his gray head to go down in peace to Sheol.
en.R: Be wise in the way you deal with him. Do not let him live out his old age and go down to the grave in peace.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the realm of the dead, pictured as below the earth, where everyone goes at death (Genesis 37:35; 1 Samuel 2:6). To go down to Sheol is simply to die.

decisions.choice: bring down his gray head in peace: let him die of old age
decisions.reason: The gray head stands for an old man (Genesis 42:38; 44:29). To go down to Sheol in peace is to die a quiet, natural death. Joab was by now old, and David asks that he not be left to die that way.

decisions.choice: act according to your wisdom: deal with the blood guilt
decisions.reason: Innocent blood left unpunished brought guilt on the land and on those responsible for justice (Numbers 35:33; Deuteronomy 19:11-13). David had cursed Joab's house for Abner's death but never punished him (2 Samuel 3:28-39). Solomon is to judge how and when to act; verses 31-33 show that he sees Joab's death as removing that guilt from David's house.

decisions.choice: wisdom: skill in judging and acting
decisions.reason: Wisdom here is practical: knowing what to do in a hard case. It is the gift Solomon will ask for (3:9) and use in judgment (3:28).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the place of the dead, as elsewhere at that level.

source.text: וְלִבְנֵ֨י בַרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־חֶ֔סֶד וְהָי֖וּ בְּאֹכְלֵ֣י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ כִּי־כֵן֙ קָרְב֣וּ אֵלַ֔י בְּבָרְחִ֕י מִפְּנֵ֖י אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: But to [the] sons of Barzillai the Gileadite you shall do steadfast love, and they shall be among [those] eating [at] your table, for so they drew near to me when I fled from before Absalom your brother.

en.L: But to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite show steadfast love, and let them be among those eating [at] your table, for so they drew near to me when I fled from before Absalom your brother.
en.B: But show faithful love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite; give them a place among those who eat at your table, for they came to my side in just that way when I was fleeing from your brother Absalom.
en.R: But show faithful love to the sons of Barzillai from Gilead. Let them be among the people who eat at your table. They stood by me in the same way when I was running away from your brother Absalom.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal kindness that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word names the loyal goodness that people bound to each other show, especially when it is not owed by law. Barzillai's family showed it to David, and David asks Solomon to return it.

decisions.choice: Barzillai: the old man who fed David at Mahanaim
decisions.reason: When David fled from Absalom, Barzillai of Rogelim in Gilead brought food and supplies to his army (2 Samuel 17:27-29). David offered to keep him in Jerusalem; he declined because of his age and sent Chimham in his place (2 Samuel 19:32-41).

decisions.choice: among those eating at your table: a place among the king's honored dependents
decisions.reason: To eat at the king's table was to be provided for by the king and given a place of honor at court, as David did for Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:7-13) and offered to Barzillai (2 Samuel 19:34).

decisions.choice: for so they drew near to me: their kindness came first
decisions.reason: "So" points back to what Solomon is to do: they came to David with the same kind of help when he needed it. Solomon's kindness repays theirs.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "faithful love", as everywhere this word is rendered at those levels.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה עִ֠מְּךָ שִֽׁמְעִ֨י בֶן־גֵּרָ֥א בֶן־הַיְמִינִי֮ מִבַּחֻרִים֒ וְה֤וּא קִֽלְלַ֨נִי֙ קְלָלָ֣ה נִמְרֶ֔צֶת בְּי֖וֹם לֶכְתִּ֣י מַחֲנָ֑יִם וְהֽוּא־יָרַ֤ד לִקְרָאתִי֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וָאֶשָּׁ֨בַֽע ל֤וֹ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם־אֲמִֽיתְךָ֖ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, with you [is] Shimei son of Gera the Benjaminite from Bahurim, and he cursed me [with a] grievous curse on [the] day of my going [to] Mahanaim; and he came down to meet me [at] the Jordan, and I swore to him by Yahweh, saying, If I put you to death with the sword.

en.L: And look, with you [is] Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went [to] Mahanaim; but he came down to meet me [at] the Jordan, and I swore to him by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
en.B: There is also Shimei son of Gera with you, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He hurled bitter curses at me on the day I set out for Mahanaim. But he came down to the Jordan to meet me, and I gave him my oath by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
en.R: Shimei son of Gera is also still here with you. He is the man from the tribe of Benjamin who comes from Bahurim. He shouted terrible curses at me on the day I went to Mahanaim. Later he came down to the Jordan River to meet me, and I made a promise to him in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I said, 'I will not kill you with the sword.'

decisions.choice: Shimei's curse and David's oath
decisions.reason: As David fled from Absalom, Shimei of Saul's clan threw stones at him and cursed him as a man of blood (2 Samuel 16:5-13). When David returned, Shimei hurried down to the Jordan to beg forgiveness, and David swore that he would not die (2 Samuel 19:17-24).

decisions.choice: grievous: bitter, painful
decisions.reason: The word means severe or painful (Micah 2:10; Job 6:25). Shimei's curse was a deep insult, and cursing the ruler of God's people was forbidden (Exodus 22:27).

decisions.choice: if I put you to death: an oath meaning "I will not"
decisions.reason: A Hebrew oath often begins "if I do this..." and leaves the self-curse unsaid; the sense is a firm promise not to do it.

decisions.choice: with you: near you, within your reach
decisions.reason: Shimei is still alive and close at hand. Bahurim was a village east of Jerusalem on the road to the Jordan (2 Samuel 16:5).

decisions.choice: the man from the tribe of Benjamin; the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Benjaminite" and adds that the Jordan is a river.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תְּנַקֵּ֔הוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם אָ֑תָּה וְיָֽדַעְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לּ֔וֹ וְהוֹרַדְתָּ֧ אֶת־שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּדָ֖ם שְׁאֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: But now do not hold him innocent, for a wise man [are] you, and you will know what you shall do to him, and you shall bring down his gray head with blood [to] Sheol.

en.L: But now do not hold him innocent, for you [are] a wise man, and you will know what you should do to him, and you will bring down his gray head with blood [to] Sheol."
en.B: But now, do not treat him as innocent. You are a wise man; you will know what to do to him. Bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood."
en.R: But do not let him go unpunished. You are wise, and you will know what to do with him. He is an old man now, but see that he dies a violent death and goes down to the grave."

decisions.choice: do not hold him innocent: do not let him go unpunished
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone as free of guilt, and so to leave him unpunished (Exodus 20:7; 34:7).

decisions.choice: but now: David's oath does not cancel Shimei's guilt
decisions.reason: David's oath bound David himself (verse 8). He now leaves Shimei's case to Solomon's judgment. The narrator does not comment on whether this was right; verses 36-46 show Solomon giving Shimei terms he could keep and acting only when he broke them.

decisions.choice: bring down his gray head with blood to Sheol: let him die a violent death
decisions.reason: The words answer verse 6 and contrast with "in peace" there: the old man is not to die a quiet death but to be put to death for his crime.

decisions.choice: He is an old man now, but see that he dies a violent death
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the gray head brought down with blood.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down David with his fathers, and he was buried in [the] city of David.

en.L: And David lay down with his fathers, and he was buried in the City of David.
en.B: Then David rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David.
en.R: Then David died and was buried in the City of David.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: This is the formula Kings uses for the death of a king (11:43; 14:20, 31). It speaks of death as lying down to rest and joining those who went before.

decisions.choice: the City of David: the old stronghold of Zion in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: David captured the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and named it the City of David (2 Samuel 5:7, 9). It was the oldest part of Jerusalem, on the hill south of the later temple, and the kings of Judah were buried there (11:43; 14:31).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings.

source.text: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ דָּוִד֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם מָלַ֔ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And the days which reigned David over Israel [were] forty years; in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years.

en.L: And the days that David reigned over Israel [were] forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
en.B: David's reign over Israel lasted forty years: seven of them he reigned in Hebron, and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
en.R: David was king over Israel for forty years. He ruled in Hebron for seven years and in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

decisions.choice: forty years: a round total
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:4-5 gives seven years and six months in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. The summary here rounds the Hebron years.

decisions.choice: over Israel: the whole reign
decisions.reason: In Hebron David reigned at first over Judah only (2 Samuel 2:4, 11). The summary counts his whole reign as his reign over Israel.

source.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֕ה יָשַׁ֕ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֖א דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַתִּכֹּ֥ן מַלְכֻת֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And Solomon sat on [the] throne of David his father, and was established his kingdom greatly.

en.L: And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was established greatly.
en.B: So Solomon took his seat on the throne of his father David, and his royal rule was made very firm.
en.R: Solomon now ruled as king in his father David's place, and his rule was very secure.

decisions.choice: sat on the throne: reigned
decisions.reason: To sit on the throne is to rule as king (1:13, 17).

decisions.choice: his kingdom was established: Yahweh's promise kept
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Yahweh's promise to David, "I will establish his kingdom" (2 Samuel 7:12). The chapter ends with the same verb (verse 46): the story in between shows how Solomon's rule was made firm.

decisions.choice: kingdom: royal rule
decisions.reason: The word means kingship or reign, the king's power to rule, more than the land he rules.

decisions.choice: Solomon now ruled as king in his father David's place
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of sitting on the throne.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־חַגֵּ֗יתאֶל־בַּת־שֶׁ֨בַע֙ אֵם־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הֲשָׁל֣וֹם בֹּאֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Adonijah son of Haggith to Bathsheba mother of Solomon, and she said, [In] peace your coming? And he said, Peace.

en.L: And Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she said, "[Is] your coming [in] peace?" And he said, "Peace."
en.B: Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked, "Have you come in peace?" "Yes, in peace," he answered.
en.R: Some time later Adonijah son of Haggith came to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked him, "Is this a friendly visit?" "Yes, it is," he answered.

decisions.choice: Adonijah son of Haggith: Solomon's older half-brother and rival
decisions.reason: Adonijah was David's fourth son (2 Samuel 3:4) and the oldest still living. He had tried to make himself king while David was dying, and Solomon spared him on condition that he behave well (1:5-10, 50-53).

decisions.choice: in peace: with friendly intent
decisions.reason: To ask whether someone comes in peace is to ask whether he means well or brings trouble (1 Samuel 16:4-5; 2 Kings 9:17-22). Bathsheba has reason to be wary of the man who tried to take the throne from her son.

decisions.choice: Is this a friendly visit? Yes, it is
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question about peace in everyday words. "Some time later" marks the new scene, which the Hebrew begins with its usual "and".

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דָּבָ֥ר לִ֖י אֵלָ֑יִךְ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, A word [is] to me to you. And she said, Speak.

en.L: And he said, "I have a word for you." And she said, "Speak."
en.B: Then he said, "I have something to say to you." "Say it," she replied.
en.R: He said, "I want to ask you something." She said, "Go ahead."

decisions.choice: a word: a matter to raise
decisions.reason: The word can mean a matter or piece of business. Here it is a request, as verse 16 makes plain.

decisions.choice: Say it; Go ahead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the one-word command in the way a person would answer in conversation.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַ֤תְּ יָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּי־לִי֙ הָיְתָ֣ה הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וְעָלַ֞י שָׂ֧מוּ כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לִמְלֹ֑ךְ וַתִּסֹּ֤ב הַמְּלוּכָה֙ וַתְּהִ֣י לְאָחִ֔י כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה הָ֥יְתָה לּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, You know that to me was the kingdom, and on me set all Israel their faces to reign; and turned the kingdom and became [my] brother's, for from Yahweh it was his.

en.L: And he said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set their faces on me to reign; but the kingdom turned around and became my brother's, for it was his from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He said, "You know that the kingship was mine. All Israel looked to me to be king. But the kingship changed hands and went to my brother, because it came to him from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine. All the people of Israel expected me to be their king. But things changed, and the kingdom went to my brother instead, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it to him.

decisions.choice: the kingdom was mine: Adonijah's own claim
decisions.reason: Adonijah speaks as the oldest living son, who might expect to succeed (1:5-6). His claim that "all Israel" looked to him goes beyond what chapter 1 shows, where only some of the court followed him (1:7-10, 19). The words are his, not the narrator's.

decisions.choice: set their faces on me: looked to me, expected me
decisions.reason: To set one's face on someone is to look to him with expectation.

decisions.choice: for it was his from Yahweh: Adonijah admits Yahweh's choice
decisions.reason: Yahweh had loved Solomon from birth (2 Samuel 12:24-25), and David had sworn that Solomon would reign (1:13, 30). Adonijah grants this, perhaps to sound harmless before making his request.

decisions.choice: the kingship
decisions.reason: Balanced says "kingship" because the word means the royal office, which can pass from one man to another.

decisions.choice: things changed
decisions.reason: Readable puts the picture of the kingdom turning around in plain words.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁאֵלָ֤ה אַחַת֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֵ֣ל מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־תָּשִׁ֖בִי אֶת־פָּנָ֑י וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דַּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And now one request I [am] asking from you; do not turn back my face. And she said to him, Speak.

en.L: And now I am asking one request from you; do not turn back my face." And she said to him, "Speak."
en.B: Now I have one request to ask of you. Do not refuse me." "Say it," she replied.
en.R: Now I have one thing to ask you. Please do not say no." She said, "Go ahead."

decisions.choice: do not turn back my face: do not refuse me
decisions.reason: To turn back someone's face is to send him away with his request denied (verse 20; Psalm 132:10).

decisions.choice: Do not refuse me; Please do not say no
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִמְרִי־נָא֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְיִתֶּן־לִ֛י אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֥ג הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֖ית לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Speak please to Solomon the king, for not will he turn back your face, and let him give to me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.

en.L: And he said, "Please speak to Solomon the king, for he will not turn back your face, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife."
en.B: He said, "Please ask King Solomon, for he will not refuse you, to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."
en.R: He said, "Please ask King Solomon to let me marry Abishag, the young woman from Shunem. He will not say no to you."

decisions.choice: Abishag: the young woman who cared for David in his last days
decisions.reason: Abishag was brought to keep the old king warm and serve him, but David did not have relations with her (1:1-4, 15).

decisions.choice: the request: more than a private wish
decisions.reason: In Israel and its neighbors, taking a dead or fallen king's women could be a claim to his place (2 Samuel 3:7; 12:8; 16:21-22). Abishag belonged to David's household, so marrying her would strengthen Adonijah's claim to the throne. The narrator does not say what Adonijah intended, but Solomon reads the request this way (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the Shunammite: from the town of Shunem
decisions.reason: Shunem was a town of Issachar in the Jezreel Valley (Joshua 19:18; 1 Samuel 28:4).

decisions.choice: He will not say no to you
decisions.reason: Readable moves the reason to the end so that the request comes first and reads simply.

source.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר בַּת־שֶׁ֖בַע ט֑וֹב אָנֹכִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Bathsheba, Good; I will speak for you to the king.

en.L: And Bathsheba said, "Good; I will speak for you to the king."
en.B: "Very well," said Bathsheba. "I will speak on your behalf to the king."
en.R: "All right," Bathsheba said. "I will talk to the king for you."

decisions.choice: for you: on your behalf
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "for" or "about". Bathsheba agrees to speak for him. The text does not say whether she saw what the request could mean or chose not to see it.

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֤א בַת־שֶׁ֨בַע֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לְדַבֶּר־ל֖וֹ עַל־אֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיָּקָם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לִקְרָאתָ֜הּ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֣חוּ לָ֗הּ וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כִּסֵּא֙ לְאֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב לִֽימִינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Bathsheba to the king Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah; and rose the king to meet her and bowed down to her and sat on his throne and placed a throne for [the] mother of the king, and she sat at his right.

en.L: And Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her, and he sat on his throne and set a throne for the mother of the king, and she sat at his right [hand].
en.B: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him on behalf of Adonijah. The king stood up to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
en.R: So Bathsheba went to talk with King Solomon for Adonijah. The king got up to welcome her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had another throne put there for his mother. She sat down at his right side.

decisions.choice: a throne for the king's mother at his right: the honored place of the queen mother
decisions.reason: The king's mother held a high place at the court of Judah (15:13; Jeremiah 13:18). The right hand was the place of greatest honor beside a king (Psalm 110:1).

decisions.choice: the king rose and bowed down to her: the reversal of chapter 1
decisions.reason: When Bathsheba came to David she bowed down to the king (1:16, 31). Now the king bows to her. The scene shows her new standing, and so the weight her request will carry.

decisions.choice: set a throne: had one set
decisions.reason: The king himself is the subject, but it was surely done at his order.

decisions.choice: had a throne set; had another throne put there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "had" because the king ordered it rather than carrying the seat himself.

source.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שְׁאֵלָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֶ֣לֶת מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־תָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּֽאמֶר־לָ֤הּ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שַׁאֲלִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֥י לֹֽא־אָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־פָּנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, One small request I [am] asking from you; do not turn back my face. And said to her the king, Ask, my mother, for not will I turn back your face.

en.L: And she said, "I am asking one small request from you; do not turn back my face." And the king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not turn back your face."
en.B: She said, "I have one small request to ask of you. Do not refuse me." The king answered her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not refuse you."
en.R: She said, "I have one small favor to ask you. Please do not say no." The king answered, "Ask me, Mother. I will not say no to you."

decisions.choice: small: as she sees it
decisions.reason: Bathsheba calls the request small. The king will see it very differently (verse 22).

decisions.choice: turn back the face: refuse
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

decisions.choice: favor
decisions.reason: Readable says "favor" for the request, a common word for something asked of a person in power.

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר יֻתַּ֖ן אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֣ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֑ית לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֥הוּ אָחִ֖יךָ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Let be given Abishag the Shunammite to Adonijah your brother as wife.

en.L: And she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as a wife."
en.B: She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given in marriage to your brother Adonijah."
en.R: She said, "Let your brother Adonijah marry Abishag, the young woman from Shunem."

decisions.choice: let be given: a request that leaves the giver unnamed
decisions.reason: The verb is passive. Bathsheba asks that Abishag be given, without saying in so many words that Solomon must give David's woman away.

decisions.choice: your brother: Adonijah presented as family
decisions.reason: Bathsheba speaks of Adonijah as Solomon's brother, not as his rival. Solomon answers by speaking of him as his older brother, the one with a claim to the throne (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Let your brother Adonijah marry
decisions.reason: Readable puts the passive request in active words.

source.text: וַיַּעַן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִמּ֗וֹ וְלָמָה֩ אַ֨תְּ שֹׁאֶ֜לֶת אֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֤ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּית֙ לַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ וְשַֽׁאֲלִי־לוֹ֙ אֶת־הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָחִ֖י הַגָּד֣וֹל מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְלוֹ֙ וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And answered the king Solomon and said to his mother, And why [are] you asking Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? And ask for him the kingdom, for he [is] my brother, the older than me; and for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah.

en.L: And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, "And why are you asking Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him too, for he [is] my brother, older than I; yes, for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"
en.B: King Solomon answered his mother, "Why are you asking for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him, since he is my older brother. Ask it for him, and for Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah too!"
en.R: King Solomon answered his mother, "Why are you asking me to give Abishag to Adonijah? You might as well ask me to give him the kingdom too! After all, he is my older brother. Ask it for him, and for Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah too!"

decisions.choice: ask the kingdom for him: bitter irony
decisions.reason: Solomon does not mean the command. He means that the request for Abishag is a request for the throne in another form, and he says so with sharp irony.

decisions.choice: Abishag and the kingdom: a claim to David's place
decisions.reason: See verse 17. To Solomon, giving David's woman to his older brother would be to hand him a claim on David's throne.

decisions.choice: and for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab: the Hebrew as it stands
alternatives: and on his side are Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is abrupt: Solomon adds the two men who had backed Adonijah's earlier attempt (1:7), as if they too would share in the kingdom. Some ancient translations read it differently, as "and on his side are Abiathar the priest and Joab". The meaning is much the same: the request revives the whole party that tried to take the throne.

decisions.choice: You might as well ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the irony, so that the words are not taken as a real command.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַע֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁ֔וֹ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And swore the king Solomon by Yahweh, saying, Thus may do to me God and thus may he add, for at [the cost of] his life has spoken Adonijah this word.

en.L: And King Solomon swore by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Thus may God do to me, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at [the cost of] his life!
en.B: Then King Solomon swore by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "May God deal with me ever so severely if this request does not cost Adonijah his life!
en.R: Then King Solomon made a promise in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "May God punish me terribly if Adonijah does not pay for this request with his life!

decisions.choice: thus may God do to me and more: an oath with a self-curse
decisions.reason: The speaker calls on God to punish him, and more, if he does not do what he swears (Ruth 1:17; 1 Samuel 3:17; 2 Samuel 3:9).

decisions.choice: at the cost of his life: the request will cost him his life
decisions.reason: The words in his own life mean that Adonijah has staked his life on this request, and will lose it.

decisions.choice: this word: this request
decisions.reason: The word means what Adonijah has asked through Bathsheba.

decisions.choice: May God deal with me ever so severely; May God punish me terribly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of the oath formula, as in 2 Samuel 3:9.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַי־יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱכִינַ֗נִי וַיּֽוֹשִׁיבַ֨נִי֙ עַל־כִּסֵּא֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֛י בַּ֖יִת כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם יוּמַ֖ת אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, [as] lives Yahweh who established me and seated me on [the] throne of David my father and who made for me a house as he spoke, for today shall be put to death Adonijah.

en.L: And now, [as] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who established me and seated me on the throne of David my father, and who made me a house as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, surely today Adonijah will be put to death."
en.B: Now, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who has made me secure and seated me on the throne of my father David, and has made me a house as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, Adonijah will be put to death today!"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made me secure as king and put me on my father David's throne. He has kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise and given my family a lasting rule. As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, Adonijah will be put to death today!"

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: an oath
decisions.reason: To swear by the life of Yahweh is to call the living God as witness that one will do what one says (1 Samuel 14:39; 20:3).

decisions.choice: made me a house: gave me a royal line
decisions.reason: "House" here means a dynasty, a line of kings, as in Yahweh's promise to David (2 Samuel 7:11, 16). Solomon may already have had a son: Rehoboam was born about a year before Solomon became king (14:21 with 11:42).

decisions.choice: as he promised: the word to David
decisions.reason: Solomon sees his accession as the keeping of Yahweh's promise (2 Samuel 7:12-13; 1:48).

decisions.choice: The LORD has made me secure ... As surely as the LORD lives
decisions.reason: Readable puts the description of what Yahweh has done before the oath, so that the oath and its content stay together in one short sentence.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד בְּנָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Solomon by [the] hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he fell on him, and he died.

en.L: And King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he fell upon him, and he died.
en.B: So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck Adonijah down, and he died.
en.R: So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Benaiah killed Adonijah.

decisions.choice: fell upon him: attacked and killed him
decisions.reason: To fall upon someone is to strike him down (verses 29, 31, 34, 46; Judges 8:21; 2 Samuel 1:15).

decisions.choice: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: commander of the royal guard
decisions.reason: Benaiah was a famous warrior who commanded David's bodyguard (2 Samuel 8:18; 23:20-23) and stood with Solomon against Adonijah (1:8, 38).

decisions.choice: sent by the hand of: sent through
decisions.reason: The king gave the order and Benaiah carried it out.

decisions.choice: Adonijah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Adonijah so that it is clear who was killed.

source.text: וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲנָתֹת֙ לֵ֣ךְ עַל־שָׂדֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ מָ֖וֶת אָ֑תָּה וּבַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה לֹ֣א אֲמִיתֶ֗ךָ כִּֽי־נָשָׂ֜אתָ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ לִפְנֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וְכִ֣י הִתְעַנִּ֔יתָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְעַנָּ֖ה אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Abiathar the priest said the king, [To] Anathoth go, to your fields, for a man of death [are] you; but on this day not will I put you to death, because you carried [the] ark of [the] Lord Yahweh before David my father, and because you were afflicted in all that was afflicted my father.

en.L: And to Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you [are] a man of death; but on this day I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}} before David my father, and because you suffered in all that my father suffered."
en.B: To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to your fields at Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you bore the ark of the {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}} before my father David and shared in all the hardships my father endured."
en.R: The king said to Abiathar the priest, "Go home to your fields in Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not kill you now. You carried the ark of the {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}} for my father David, and you suffered with my father through all his troubles."

decisions.choice: a man of death: one who deserves to die
decisions.reason: The phrase marks a man as worthy of death, like "son of death" (1 Samuel 26:16; 2 Samuel 12:5). Abiathar had backed Adonijah's attempt on the throne (1:7, 25).

decisions.choice: Anathoth: a town of priests
decisions.reason: Anathoth was a town of Benjamin given to the priests (Joshua 21:18), a few miles north of Jerusalem. The prophet Jeremiah later came from its priests (Jeremiah 1:1).

decisions.choice: carried the ark; suffered with my father
decisions.reason: Abiathar alone escaped when Saul killed the priests of Nob, and he stayed with David through his years as a fugitive (1 Samuel 22:20-23; 23:6). With Zadok he carried the ark when David fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 15:24-29).

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh: Yahweh as master
decisions.reason: The title joins "Lord", meaning master, to the divine name. It is the usual form of the title in the books of Samuel and Kings and the prophets.

decisions.choice: on this day: for now
decisions.reason: Solomon spares Abiathar's life at this time but does not cancel the sentence he says Abiathar deserves.

decisions.choice: for my father David
decisions.reason: Readable says "for" where the Hebrew has "before", meaning in David's service and presence.

source.text: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־אֶבְיָתָ֔ר מִהְי֥וֹת כֹּהֵ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְמַלֵּא֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר עַל־בֵּ֥ית עֵלִ֖י בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And drove out Solomon Abiathar from being priest to Yahweh, to fulfill [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke concerning [the] house of Eli in Shiloh.

en.L: And Solomon drove out Abiathar from being priest to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to fulfill the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
en.B: So Solomon removed Abiathar from serving as priest of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This fulfilled the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken about the house of Eli at Shiloh.
en.R: So Solomon removed Abiathar from his work as a priest of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This made come true what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said about Eli's family in Shiloh.

decisions.choice: the word against the house of Eli: 1 Samuel 2:27-36 and 3:11-14
decisions.reason: A man of God told Eli at Shiloh that his family would lose the priesthood and that Yahweh would raise up a faithful priest in its place (1 Samuel 2:27-36), and Yahweh confirmed it to the boy Samuel (1 Samuel 3:11-14). Abiathar was Eli's descendant through Phinehas, Ahitub and Ahimelech (1 Samuel 14:3; 22:20). With his removal the line of Eli loses the high priesthood, and Zadok holds it alone (verse 35).

decisions.choice: to fulfill: the result Yahweh intended
decisions.reason: The narrator says what Solomon's act achieved in Yahweh's plan, not what Solomon had in mind. Solomon gives his own reasons in verse 26.

decisions.choice: drove out: removed from office and sent away
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive out or banish. Abiathar is sent from Jerusalem and from his place as priest.

decisions.choice: This fulfilled; This made come true
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence for the fulfilment, so that it reads as the narrator's comment.

source.text: וְהַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ בָּ֣אָה עַד־יוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֣י יוֹאָ֗ב נָטָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיָּ֔ה וְאַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לֹ֣א נָטָ֑ה וַיָּ֤נָס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the report came to Joab — for Joab had turned after Adonijah, but after Absalom he had not turned — and fled Joab to [the] tent of Yahweh and took hold of [the] horns of the altar.

en.L: And the report came to Joab, for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though after Absalom he had not turned; and Joab fled to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and took hold of the horns of the altar.
en.B: When the news reached Joab, since he had sided with Adonijah, though he had not sided with Absalom, Joab fled to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and grasped the horns of the altar.
en.R: Joab heard the news. He had taken Adonijah's side, though he had never taken Absalom's side. So he ran to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and grabbed the horns at the corners of the altar, hoping to be safe there.

decisions.choice: took hold of the horns of the altar: asked for sanctuary
decisions.reason: The altar had horn-shaped corners (Exodus 27:2). A man who took hold of them put himself under God's protection and asked not to be killed, as Adonijah had done (1:50-53). But the law gave no refuge at the altar to a man who had murdered on purpose: "from my altar you shall take him to die" (Exodus 21:14). Joab is that kind of man (verses 5, 31-32).

decisions.choice: the tent of Yahweh: the tent for the ark in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: This was the tent David pitched for the ark in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:17), where Zadok anointed Solomon with oil from it (1:39). The temple had not yet been built.

decisions.choice: turned after: took the side of
decisions.reason: To turn after someone is to follow him as his supporter. Joab had stood with David against Absalom, but he backed Adonijah against Solomon (1:7).

decisions.choice: the report: news of what Solomon had done
decisions.reason: The report is not described; the context suggests news of Adonijah's death and Abiathar's banishment, which told Joab he was next.

decisions.choice: the horns at the corners of the altar, hoping to be safe there
decisions.reason: Readable says where the horns were and why Joab held them, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader's knowledge.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֞ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כִּ֣י נָ֤ס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע לֵאמֹ֖ר לֵ֥ךְ פְּגַע־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to king Solomon that had fled Joab to [the] tent of Yahweh, and look, [he is] beside the altar; and sent Solomon Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall on him.

en.L: And it was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and look, [he is] beside the altar. And Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, fall upon him."
en.B: King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and was there beside the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with the order, "Go and strike him down."
en.R: Someone told King Solomon that Joab had run to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and was by the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada and told him, "Go and kill him."

decisions.choice: fall upon him: strike him down
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

decisions.choice: look, beside the altar: the report as the messengers gave it
decisions.reason: "Look" brings the reader into the moment of the report: Joab is at the altar.

decisions.choice: Solomon sent Benaiah: the shorter Hebrew text
alternatives: a longer text with Solomon's question and Joab's answer
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text moves straight to Solomon's order. The ancient Greek translation adds that Solomon sent to ask Joab why he had fled to the altar, and Joab answered that he was afraid of the king and had fled to Yahweh. The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: Go and kill him
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the idiom.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א בְנָיָ֜הוּ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ צֵ֔א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר׀לֹ֖א כִּ֣י פֹ֣ה אָמ֑וּת וַיָּ֨שֶׁב בְּנָיָ֤הוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־דִבֶּ֥ר יוֹאָ֖ב וְכֹ֥ה עָנָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Benaiah to [the] tent of Yahweh and said to him, Thus says the king, Come out. And he said, No, for here I will die. And brought back Benaiah [to] the king word, saying, Thus spoke Joab and thus he answered me.

en.L: And Benaiah came to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said to him, "Thus says the king, 'Come out.'" And he said, "No, for here I will die." And Benaiah brought back word [to] the king, saying, "Thus Joab spoke, and thus he answered me."
en.B: Benaiah went to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said to him, "The king says this: 'Come out!'" But he said, "No, I will die here." Benaiah took word back to the king: "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."
en.R: Benaiah went to the tent of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said to Joab, "The king orders you to come out!" But Joab answered, "No! I will die right here." Benaiah went back to the king and told him what Joab had said.

decisions.choice: no, for here I will die: Joab refuses to leave
decisions.reason: Joab will not leave the altar. If he must die, it will be there, perhaps in the hope that the king will not dare to kill a man at Yahweh's altar.

decisions.choice: Benaiah brought back word: he does not act at once
decisions.reason: Benaiah does not kill Joab at the altar on his own authority but returns for the king's decision.

decisions.choice: The king orders you to come out
decisions.reason: Readable puts the messenger's formula and the command into one plain sentence, and names Joab.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲשֵׂה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר וּפְגַע־בּ֖וֹ וּקְבַרְתּ֑וֹ וַהֲסִירֹ֣תָ׀דְּמֵ֣י חִנָּ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁפַ֣ךְ יוֹאָ֔ב מֵעָלַ֕י וּמֵעַ֖ל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the king, Do as he has spoken, and fall on him and bury him, and you will remove [the] blood without cause which shed Joab from on me and from on [the] house of my father.

en.L: And the king said to him, "Do as he has spoken: fall upon him and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the blood without cause that Joab shed.
en.B: The king said to him, "Do as he said. Strike him down and bury him, and so take away from me and from my father's house the guilt of the blood that Joab shed without cause.
en.R: The king told him, "Do what he said. Kill him and bury him. Then my family and I will no longer carry the guilt for the people Joab killed for no reason.

decisions.choice: remove the blood without cause: take away the guilt of innocent blood
decisions.reason: Blood shed without cause brought guilt on the community until justice was done (Numbers 35:33; Deuteronomy 19:10-13; 21:8-9). Because David had left Joab unpunished, that guilt rested on David's house. Joab's death removes it.

decisions.choice: do as he has spoken: take him at his word
decisions.reason: Joab said he would die there (verse 30); the king tells Benaiah to let it be so.

decisions.choice: bury him: an honor even for the executed
decisions.reason: Burial was not denied him. To be left unburied was a further disgrace (Deuteronomy 21:23; 2 Kings 9:34-35).

decisions.choice: the guilt for the people Joab killed for no reason
decisions.reason: Readable explains "blood" as the guilt for killing.

source.text: וְהֵשִׁיב֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־דָּמ֜וֹ עַל־רֹאשׁ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגַ֣ע בִּשְׁנֵֽי־אֲ֠נָשִׁים צַדִּקִ֨ים וְטֹבִ֤ים מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ וַיַּהַרְגֵ֣ם בַּחֶ֔רֶב וְאָבִ֥י דָוִ֖ד לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע אֶת־אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־נֵר֙ שַׂר־צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־עֲמָשָׂ֥א בֶן־יֶ֖תֶר שַׂר־צְבָ֥א יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will bring back Yahweh his blood on his head, who fell on two men righteous and better than he and killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know: Abner son of Ner, commander of [the] army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of [the] army of Judah.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring back his blood on his own head, because he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring his blood back on his own head, because without my father David's knowledge he attacked two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will make Joab pay for the blood he shed. He attacked two men who were more honest and better than he was, and he killed them with his sword. My father David did not know about it. They were Abner son of Ner, Israel's army commander, and Amasa son of Jether, Judah's army commander.

decisions.choice: bring back his blood on his head: make the guilt fall on the one who caused it
decisions.reason: The guilt of the blood Joab shed returns on him, so that he, not David's house, bears it (Joshua 2:19; 2 Samuel 1:16).

decisions.choice: more righteous and better: more in the right
decisions.reason: "Righteous" here means in the right, innocent in comparison (1 Samuel 24:18). Abner and Amasa had done nothing to deserve death.

decisions.choice: David did not know
decisions.reason: When Joab called Abner back to kill him, David knew nothing of it, and said so publicly (2 Samuel 3:26-28).

decisions.choice: commander of the army of Israel; of Judah
decisions.reason: Abner commanded the army of Saul and Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 2:8). Amasa commanded Absalom's army and was then appointed by David over the army in Joab's place (2 Samuel 17:25; 19:14).

decisions.choice: without my father David's knowledge
decisions.reason: Balanced brings the clause about David forward so that the list of names closes the sentence.

decisions.choice: army commander
decisions.reason: Readable uses the settled wording for this title.

source.text: וְשָׁ֤בוּ דְמֵיהֶם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וּבְרֹ֥אשׁ זַרְע֖וֹ לְעֹלָ֑ם וּלְדָוִ֡ד וּ֠לְזַרְעוֹ וּלְבֵית֨וֹ וּלְכִסְא֜וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁל֛וֹם עַד־עוֹלָ֖ם מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will return their blood on [the] head of Joab and on [the] head of his offspring forever; but to David and to his offspring and to his house and to his throne will be peace forever from with Yahweh.

en.L: And their blood will return on the head of Joab and on the head of his offspring forever; but for David and for his offspring and for his house and for his throne there will be peace forever from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: So their blood will come back on Joab's head and on the heads of his descendants forever. But for David and his descendants, his house and his throne, there will be peace from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever."
en.R: The guilt for their deaths will be on Joab and his descendants forever. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give peace to David and his descendants, his family and his kingdom, forever."

decisions.choice: their blood will return on the head of Joab: he bears the guilt
decisions.reason: As in verse 32.

decisions.choice: peace: safety and well-being
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness, safety and well-being. With the guilt removed, Yahweh will give David's line peace.

decisions.choice: there will be: a statement that may also be a wish
decisions.reason: The verb can state what will happen or express a wish, "may there be". The difference is small: either way, Solomon looks to Yahweh to keep David's house safe.

decisions.choice: the guilt for their deaths; his family and his kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable explains the blood as guilt, the house as David's family and the throne as his kingdom.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַל בְּנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיְמִתֵ֑הוּ וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּבֵית֖וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Benaiah son of Jehoiada and fell on him and killed him, and he was buried in his house in the wilderness.

en.L: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and fell upon him and put him to death, and he was buried at his house in the wilderness.
en.B: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and killed him, and he was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
en.R: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went back and killed Joab. Joab was buried on his own land in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: buried at his house in the wilderness: on his family's land
decisions.reason: To be buried at one's house means on one's own land, in the family tomb (1 Samuel 25:1). Joab's family came from Bethlehem (2 Samuel 2:32); the wilderness is likely the open country of Judah east of it.

decisions.choice: fell upon him: struck him down
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

decisions.choice: went up: went to carry out the order
decisions.reason: The verb often means to go up to a higher place; here it is Benaiah's return to the tent where Joab was.

decisions.choice: went back
decisions.reason: Readable says "went back" because Benaiah had come from the tent to the king (verse 30).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע תַּחְתָּ֖יו עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וְאֶת־צָד֤וֹק הַכֹּהֵן֙ נָתַ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תַּ֖חַת אֶבְיָתָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And put the king Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and Zadok the priest put the king in [the] place of Abiathar.

en.L: And the king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army; and Zadok the priest the king put in the place of Abiathar.
en.B: The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab's place, and he put Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.
en.R: The king made Benaiah son of Jehoiada commander of the army in place of Joab. And he gave Abiathar's place to Zadok the priest.

decisions.choice: Zadok in Abiathar's place: the faithful priest
decisions.reason: Zadok and Abiathar had served together as David's priests (2 Samuel 8:17; 15:24-29). Now Zadok alone holds the office. This fits the promise to Eli's house that Yahweh would raise up a faithful priest in place of Eli's line (1 Samuel 2:35; verse 27).

decisions.choice: and Zadok the priest the king put: a contrast
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Zadok first to set the two appointments side by side: Benaiah for Joab, Zadok for Abiathar.

decisions.choice: in Joab's place; in place of Joab
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joab, whom "his place" refers to.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֔י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ בְּֽנֵה־לְךָ֥ בַ֨יִת֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ שָׁ֑ם וְלֹֽא־תֵצֵ֥א מִשָּׁ֖ם אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king and summoned Shimei and said to him, Build for yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and not go out from there here or there.

en.L: And the king sent and called for Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there, here or there.
en.B: Then the king summoned Shimei and told him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and make your home there. Do not leave it to go anywhere at all.
en.R: Then the king sent for Shimei and told him, "Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go anywhere outside the city.

decisions.choice: live in Jerusalem: under the king's eye
decisions.reason: Shimei belonged to Saul's clan (2 Samuel 16:5), and his home was at Bahurim, on the way to Benjamin. Keeping him in Jerusalem kept him away from Saul's tribe and where the king could watch him.

decisions.choice: here or there: anywhere
decisions.reason: The pair of words means "to any place at all" (2 Kings 5:25).

decisions.choice: terms instead of a sentence
decisions.reason: Solomon does not put Shimei to death at once, as David's words might have allowed (verse 9). He gives him terms that he can keep, and his life depends on keeping them.

decisions.choice: anywhere at all; anywhere outside the city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the paired words.

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְעָֽבַרְתָּ֙ אֶת־נַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת דָּמְךָ֖ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, on [the] day of your going out and you cross the wadi of Kidron, knowing you shall know that dying you shall die; your blood will be on your head.

en.L: And on the day you go out and cross the Wadi Kidron, know for certain that you will surely die; your blood will be on your own head."
en.B: On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, you may be certain you will die. Your blood will be on your own head."
en.R: If you ever leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you can be sure that you will die. It will be your own fault."

decisions.choice: the Wadi Kidron: the valley east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Kidron is the valley between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives, dry except in the rainy season. Crossing it was the way east toward Bahurim and Benjamin, the way David went when he fled (2 Samuel 15:23; 16:5).

decisions.choice: know for certain that you will surely die: emphatic forms
decisions.reason: Both verbs are doubled in Hebrew for emphasis, as in Genesis 2:17. The warning leaves no room for doubt.

decisions.choice: your blood will be on your own head: you will be to blame
decisions.reason: If he dies, the guilt for his death will be his own, not the king's (Joshua 2:19; 2 Samuel 1:16).

decisions.choice: It will be your own fault
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the idiom.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְעִ֤י לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ ט֣וֹב הַדָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב שִׁמְעִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Shimei to the king, Good [is] the word; as has spoken my lord the king, so will do your servant. And lived Shimei in Jerusalem many days.

en.L: And Shimei said to the king, "The word [is] good; as my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.
en.B: Shimei answered the king, "What you say is fair. Your servant will do just as my lord the king has said." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
en.R: Shimei answered the king, "That is fair. Your servant will do just what you have said, my lord the king." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.

decisions.choice: the word is good: the terms are fair
decisions.reason: Shimei accepts the king's terms as fair and agrees to them.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way to say "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as the king's servant was the courteous way to address a superior (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7).

decisions.choice: your servant
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "your servant", as the courteous form of address it is.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וַיִּבְרְח֤וּ שְׁנֵֽי־עֲבָדִים֙ לְשִׁמְעִ֔י אֶל־אָכִ֥ישׁ בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ גַּ֑ת וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לְשִׁמְעִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּגַֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] end of three years, and fled two slaves of Shimei to Achish son of Maacah king of Gath; and they told Shimei, saying, Look, your slaves [are] in Gath.

en.L: And it was at the end of three years that two slaves of Shimei fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, "Look, your slaves [are] in Gath."
en.B: But three years later two slaves belonging to Shimei ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath."
en.R: But three years later, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, the king of Gath. Someone told Shimei, "Your slaves are in Gath."

decisions.choice: slaves: people Shimei owned
decisions.reason: These were Shimei's own slaves, his property, who ran away from him. The law forbade handing a runaway slave back to his master (Deuteronomy 23:16-17), but Shimei goes after them.

decisions.choice: Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath
decisions.reason: Gath was one of the five chief Philistine cities, southwest of Jerusalem. An Achish son of Maoch gave David refuge there (1 Samuel 27:2). Whether this is the same king, or a relative, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: they told: some people told
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the verb means that Shimei was told.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "slaves", because these were owned people who ran away, and their status is the point of the story.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם שִׁמְעִ֗י וַֽיַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ אֶת־חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ גַּ֨תָה֙ אֶל־אָכִ֔ישׁ לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְעִ֔י וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־עֲבָדָ֖יו מִגַּֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Shimei and saddled his donkey and went to Gath to Achish to seek his slaves; and went Shimei and brought his slaves from Gath.

en.L: And Shimei arose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his slaves; and Shimei went and brought his slaves from Gath.
en.B: So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to look for his slaves. Shimei went and brought his slaves back from Gath.
en.R: So Shimei saddled his donkey and went to Achish in Gath to look for his slaves. He found them and brought them back from Gath.

decisions.choice: went to Gath: outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Gath lay to the southwest, so Shimei did not cross the Kidron to the east. But he had agreed not to leave Jerusalem for any place at all (verses 36, 42), and he went far beyond it, to a foreign king.

decisions.choice: went ... went: the journey told twice
decisions.reason: The narrator tells the journey twice, once with its purpose and once with its result, so that the breach is plain.

decisions.choice: He found them
decisions.reason: Readable says that he found the slaves, which the Hebrew implies.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּי־הָלַ֨ךְ שִׁמְעִ֧י מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גַּ֖ת וַיָּשֹֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Solomon that had gone Shimei from Jerusalem [to] Gath and had returned.

en.L: And it was told to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem [to] Gath and had come back.
en.B: Word reached Solomon that Shimei had left Jerusalem for Gath and had come back.
en.R: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had left Jerusalem, gone to Gath, and come back.

decisions.choice: and had come back: he returned, but the terms were already broken
decisions.reason: Shimei did not flee; he came back. But the terms were broken the day he left the city (verse 42).

decisions.choice: Someone told
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive verb active, as in verse 39.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲל֧וֹא הִשְׁבַּעְתִּ֣יךָ בַֽיהוָ֗ה וָאָעִ֤ד בְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אָ֣נֶה וָאָ֔נָה יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלַ֛י ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king and summoned Shimei and said to him, Did not I make you swear by Yahweh and warn you, saying, On [the] day of your going out and you go here or there, knowing you shall know that dying you shall die? And you said to me, Good [is] the word; I have heard.

en.L: And the king sent and called for Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and go here or there, know for certain that you will surely die'? And you said to me, 'The word [is] good; I have heard.'
en.B: Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not have you swear by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and did I not warn you, 'The day you leave and go anywhere at all, you can be sure that you will die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is fair; I will obey.'
en.R: Then the king sent for Shimei and said to him, "I made you swear in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that you would stay here. I warned you, 'If you ever leave and go anywhere, you can be sure that you will die.' And you answered me, 'That is fair. I will obey.'

decisions.choice: made you swear by Yahweh: the terms were sworn
decisions.reason: Verses 36-38 do not mention an oath, but Solomon says that Shimei swore to the terms by Yahweh. Breaking them was therefore breaking an oath made before Yahweh (verse 43).

decisions.choice: I have heard: I accept and will obey
decisions.reason: To hear often means to listen and obey. Shimei's answer was his agreement.

decisions.choice: did I not: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of stating firmly what Shimei cannot deny.

decisions.choice: I made you swear
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

source.text: וּמַדּ֕וּעַ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֖ת שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֥יתִי עָלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And why have you not kept [the] oath of Yahweh and the command which I commanded you?

en.L: And why have you not kept the oath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the command that I commanded you?"
en.B: Why then have you failed to keep your oath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the command I gave you?"
en.R: So why did you break your promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and disobey my command?"

decisions.choice: the oath of Yahweh: the oath sworn in his name
decisions.reason: The oath was made by Yahweh's name, so he was its witness and guard (Exodus 22:10; 2 Samuel 21:7). Breaking it wronged Yahweh as well as the king.

decisions.choice: break your promise
decisions.reason: Readable says that he broke his promise, which is what failing to keep an oath means.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־שִׁמְעִ֗י אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָדַע֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ לְדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְהֵשִׁ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־רָעָתְךָ֖ בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Shimei, You know all the evil which knows your heart, which you did to David my father; and will bring back Yahweh your evil on your head.

en.L: And the king said to Shimei, "You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring back your evil on your own head.
en.B: The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your heart all the wrong you did to my father David. Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring your wrongdoing back on your own head.
en.R: The king also said to Shimei, "You know very well all the evil things you did to my father David. Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to make that evil come back on you.

decisions.choice: all the evil that your heart knows: what you know you did
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, the mind and memory. Shimei knows well what he did; he has no excuse.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will bring back your evil on your head: Yahweh's justice
decisions.reason: Solomon sees Shimei's death as Yahweh's punishment for cursing David (2 Samuel 16:5-13), not only for breaking the terms. The Hebrew word for "evil" means both the wrong done and the harm that comes back on the one who did it, and both senses are heard here.

decisions.choice: what you did to David my father
decisions.reason: See verse 8 and 2 Samuel 16:5-13.

decisions.choice: wrong; wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Balanced says "wrong" for the deed, since "evil" in modern English sounds stronger and more general.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בָּר֑וּךְ וְכִסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֛וֹן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But the king Solomon [is] blessed, and [the] throne of David will be established before Yahweh forever.

en.L: But King Solomon [will be] blessed, and the throne of David will be established before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever."
en.B: But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will stand firm before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever."
en.R: But I, King Solomon, will be blessed, and David's throne will be secure before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever."

decisions.choice: blessed: the reverse of Shimei's curse
decisions.reason: Shimei cursed David (verse 8). Now the one he cursed is shown to be blessed, and the curse falls back on the one who spoke it (Genesis 12:3; Numbers 24:9).

decisions.choice: blessed: a statement or a wish
decisions.reason: The form can be read as a statement, "is blessed" or "will be blessed", or as a wish, "may King Solomon be blessed". It sets Solomon's blessing beside Shimei's punishment.

decisions.choice: David's throne established forever: the promise of 2 Samuel 7:16
decisions.reason: Solomon repeats the words of Yahweh's promise to David: "your throne will be established forever" (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: I, King Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the king is speaking of himself.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶת־בְּנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַיִּפְגַּע־בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה נָכ֖וֹנָה בְּיַד־שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell on him, and he died. And the kingdom was established in [the] hand of Solomon.

en.L: And the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell upon him, and he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.
en.B: Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. So the kingdom was made secure in Solomon's hand.
en.R: Then the king gave Benaiah son of Jehoiada the order, and Benaiah went out and killed Shimei. Now Solomon had firm control of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: fell upon him: struck him down
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

decisions.choice: the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand: the chapter's closing frame
decisions.reason: The words pick up verse 12. With Adonijah, Joab and Shimei dead and Abiathar sent away, nothing stands in the way of Solomon's rule. The hand stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text without additions
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has long additions in this chapter, after verse 35 and after verse 46, gathering notes about Solomon's reign that are found elsewhere in Kings. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Shimei
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Shimei so that it is clear who was killed.
